Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Labour Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Economic Policy

Labour plans to establish fiscal rules requiring day-to-day costs be met by revenues and debt falling as a share of GDP by year five. They will cap corporation tax at 25%, maintain full expensing for capital investment, and reform business rates. A National Wealth Fund with £7.3 billion will invest in ports, gigafactories, steel, carbon capture, and green hydrogen. An Industrial Strategy Council will guide sectoral policy.

## Energy and Environment

Labour commits to clean power by 2030 through doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, and quadrupling offshore wind. Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland with £8.3 billion funding, will partner with private sector. They will not issue new oil and gas exploration licences but will maintain existing ones. A £6.6 billion Warm Homes Plan will upgrade five million homes. Water company reforms will include new enforcement powers and automatic fines.

## Healthcare

Labour pledges 40,000 additional NHS appointments weekly, paid through evening and weekend work. They will double CT and MRI scanners, recruit 8,500 mental health staff, and train more GPs. Dentistry reforms include 700,000 urgent appointments. Social care will move toward a National Care Service with national standards.

## Education

Proposals include 6,500 new teachers funded by ending private school tax exemptions, 3,000 new primary school nurseries, and free breakfast clubs. A curriculum review will be conducted. Skills England will coordinate training policy, and apprenticeship levy reforms will create a Growth and Skills Levy.

## Housing and Planning

Labour targets 1.5 million new homes through mandatory housing targets, planning reforms, and strategic greenbelt release. Compulsory purchase rules will be reformed. Section 21 evictions will be abolished immediately. Leasehold reform will include enacting Law Commission proposals.

## Crime and Justice

A Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee will recruit thousands of officers. Knife crime measures include banning certain blades and criminal exploitation offences. Violence against women will be addressed through specialist rape courts and domestic abuse experts in 999 rooms. Prison capacity will be expanded.

## Immigration and Borders

A Border Security Command with counter-terror powers will target smuggling gangs. The Rwanda scheme will end. Additional caseworkers will clear asylum backlogs. A new returns unit with 1,000 staff will expedite removals. Work visas will be linked to domestic training requirements.

## Constitutional Reform

Hereditary peers will lose voting rights immediately. A mandatory retirement age of 80 will apply to Lords members. Voting age will lower to 16. An Ethics and Integrity Commission will oversee ministerial standards. Devolution will deepen with new powers for combined authorities.

## Foreign Policy and Defence

Labour commits to NATO, the nuclear deterrent, and AUKUS. A Strategic Defence Review will assess capabilities. Ukraine support continues. EU relations will be reset without rejoining single market or customs union, seeking veterinary agreements and security cooperation. Palestinian statehood will be recognised.

## Workers' Rights

Within 100 days, legislation will ban zero-hours contract exploitation, end fire-and-rehire, and establish day-one employment rights. The minimum wage will account for cost of living and remove age bands. A Fair Pay Agreement in social care will be introduced.
